The Software Testing and QA internship in short

In the SkillMe Software Testing and QA internship you build QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App, a project where you build a full QA workflow around a real public web app: a test plan, real bug reports, an automated UI test suite, an API test suite, and a coverage report that proves it all holds together. In week 1 you pick a real public web app (a to-do list app, a demo e-commerce site, or similar), write a proper test plan for its core flow, and manually execute it to find real bugs. By week 4 you add an API-level automated test suite (faster and more precise than UI tests for many checks), wire both suites into CI, and produce a coverage report tying test cases back to your original test plan. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

Week by week

What each week of the Software Testing and QA internship covers

The four milestones of QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Test Planning and Manual Test Execution

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Pick a real public web app (a to-do list app, a demo e-commerce site, or similar), write a proper test plan for its core flow, and manually execute it to find real bugs. Good automation later depends on a clear, well-scoped test plan now.

    What you learn

    • Writing a test plan: scope, test cases, priorities, and pass/fail criteria
    • Designing test cases covering happy path, edge cases and negative cases
    • Manual test execution and recording results objectively
    • Distinguishing a bug from expected behavior

    What you submit

    • A written test plan with scope, environment and out-of-scope items
    • At least 15 test cases covering happy path, edge cases and negative cases
    • A test execution record with actual results and pass/fail status per case
    • A results summary with pass/fail counts and a risk assessment
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • The test plan clearly states what is in scope and explicitly what is out of scope
    • At least 15 test cases exist, spanning all three categories (happy path, edge, negative)
    • Every test case has a precondition, steps, and an expected result written before execution
    • At least one real, reproducible failure was found and confirmed against actual app behavior (not a misunderstanding of intended behavior)

    Stretch goal: Add 3 test cases specifically targeting accessibility (keyboard-only navigation through the core flow, and checking form fields have visible labels).

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Bug Reports and Regression Tracking

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn last week's found issues into proper bug reports that a real engineering team could act on without back-and-forth, and build a lightweight regression checklist to re-test after fixes. Writing a bug report that gets fixed on the first read is its own skill.

    What you learn

    • Writing a bug report with clear repro steps, expected vs actual, and severity
    • Assigning severity and priority independently and justifying each
    • Capturing evidence (screenshots, console logs, network requests)
    • Building a lightweight regression checklist for re-testing after a fix

    What you submit

    • At least 5 fully written bug reports with severity and priority justified separately
    • Evidence (screenshot or console/network capture) attached to each bug report
    • A bug tracker (spreadsheet, GitHub Issues, or board) with status tracking
    • A regression checklist of 8-10 checks covering the core flow and reported bugs
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • Each bug report has numbered repro steps specific enough that someone unfamiliar with the app could reproduce the issue on the first try
    • Severity and priority are each justified with a one-line reason, and at least one bug shows they don't match (high severity, lower priority or vice versa)
    • Every bug report has at least one piece of visual or technical evidence attached
    • The regression checklist can be executed in under 15 minutes and covers every reported bug plus the core flow

    Stretch goal: Write one bug report as a 'won't fix' status with a clear justification, practicing the judgment call of when NOT to push for a fix.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Automated UI Test Suite

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Automate the core flow from your test plan using Playwright (or Selenium), turning your manual test cases into a repeatable suite that catches regressions automatically. This is where QA work becomes engineering.

    What you learn

    • Setting up Playwright (or Selenium) with Python for browser automation
    • Writing reliable locators and avoiding flaky waits/sleeps
    • Structuring automated tests with setup/teardown and reusable helper functions
    • Generating a readable test report from an automated run

    What you submit

    • A Playwright (or Selenium) test suite automating 5-8 test cases from Week 1
    • A Page Object helper module used by the tests
    • Reliable locators with no fixed time.sleep() waits
    • An HTML (or equivalent) test report generated from a run
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • Running the suite 3 times in a row produces the same pass/fail results each time
    • At least one automated test correctly fails when run against a deliberately broken input (proving it actually checks something)
    • The suite has zero fixed time.sleep() calls used purely to wait for page state
    • An HTML test report is generated showing individual test results, not just a pass/fail count in the terminal

    Stretch goal: Add a visual regression check on one key page using Playwright's screenshot comparison (expect(page).to_have_screenshot()).

  4. Week 4 of 4

    API Test Suite, Coverage Report and CI

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Add an API-level automated test suite (faster and more precise than UI tests for many checks), wire both suites into CI, and produce a coverage report tying test cases back to your original test plan. This is the deliverable that shows a complete, professional QA process.

    What you learn

    • Writing automated API tests with requests or Postman/Newman
    • Testing status codes, response schemas and error responses at the API layer
    • Mapping test cases to a traceability/coverage report against the original test plan
    • Running both UI and API suites automatically in CI

    What you submit

    • An automated API test suite covering 4-6 endpoints with status, schema and response-time checks
    • A traceability/coverage report mapping every original test case to its automation status
    • A GitHub Actions CI workflow running both UI and API suites on every push
    • A final QA summary report with coverage percentage, bug status and known gaps
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • The API suite includes at least one 2xx success case, one 4xx error case, and one schema-shape assertion per tested endpoint
    • The coverage report accounts for all 15+ original test cases with a clear status for each
    • Pushing a commit triggers CI and both suites run automatically, with a deliberate failure confirmed to break the build
    • The final summary report states an overall automation coverage percentage and lists at least one honest known gap

    Stretch goal: Add a scheduled (cron) GitHub Actions run of the full suite once a day against the live app, separate from the on-push run, to catch regressions from the app's own side.

Is it for you?

Who the Software Testing and QA internship is for, and what you leave with

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of Test Automation, Selenium and Bug Reports and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.
  • You can start at beginner level. Week 1: Pick a real public web app (a to-do list app, a demo e-commerce site, or similar), write a proper test plan for its core flow, and manually execute it to find real bugs.
  • You want to reach intermediate+ level in four weeks. Week 4: Add an API-level automated test suite (faster and more precise than UI tests for many checks), wire both suites into CI, and produce a coverage report tying test cases back to your original test plan.
  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

Software Testing and QA internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Software Testing and QA internship?

You build QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App. Build a full QA workflow around a real public web app: a test plan, real bug reports, an automated UI test suite, an API test suite, and a coverage report that proves it all holds together. It is one project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Software Testing and QA internship?

The Software Testing and QA internship works with Test Automation, Selenium and Bug Reports. Week 1: writing a test plan: scope, test cases, priorities, and pass/fail criteria; designing test cases covering happy path, edge cases and negative cases. Week 2: writing a bug report with clear repro steps, expected vs actual, and severity; assigning severity and priority independently and justifying each. Week 3: setting up Playwright (or Selenium) with Python for browser automation; writing reliable locators and avoiding flaky waits/sleeps. Week 4: writing automated API tests with requests or Postman/Newman; testing status codes, response schemas and error responses at the API layer.

Do I need experience to apply for the Software Testing and QA internship?

You need the basics of Test Automation, Selenium and Bug Reports, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you pick a real public web app (a to-do list app, a demo e-commerce site, or similar), write a proper test plan for its core flow, and manually execute it to find real bugs. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Software Testing and QA milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of QuestGuard: Test Plan, Bugs and Automation Suite for a Real App, that means: the test plan clearly states what is in scope and explicitly what is out of scope; at least 15 test cases exist, spanning all three categories (happy path, edge, negative); every test case has a precondition, steps, and an expected result written before execution; at least one real, reproducible failure was found and confirmed against actual app behavior (not a misunderstanding of intended behavior). Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Software Testing and QA internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Wrote a full test plan with 15+ test cases spanning happy path, edge and negative scenarios; Manually executed a test plan against a real app and found a reproducible bug; Learned to write expected results before execution to avoid biased pass/fail judgments; Wrote detailed bug reports with minimized repro steps and evidence a team could act on immediately; Learned to justify severity and priority independently instead of treating them as the same thing; Built a regression checklist to quickly verify fixes without breaking other flows; Built a Playwright automated UI test suite covering happy path and edge cases; Used the Page Object pattern to keep automated tests readable and maintainable; Eliminated flaky waits by switching from fixed sleeps to explicit element-state waits; Built an automated API test suite checking status codes, schemas and response times; Produced a full traceability report mapping every test case to its automation coverage; Wired UI and API test suites into CI so every push is automatically checked for regressions.

Is the Software Testing and QA internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based and goes to the interns whose reviewed Software Testing and QA work stands out in their cohort, not to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
